Hypothesis demonstrated: pointwise simultaneous coverage 45.5%/84.8%, Bonferroni 96.3%/98.8%, sup-t 95.0%/94.3% (within 1 SE 0.011 of 95%), sup-t 0.3% wider at rho 0.3 and 17% narrower at 0.9, StepM first-step values 2.785 and 2.189 below the band's. The interpretation's per-interval sentence fails under L05-num-lab4; the rest does not overreach (it explains the 0.3% excess by finite-T tails: t_249 quantile at 0.99875 is 3.054 vs normal 3.023, limiting sup-t at rho 0.3 is 2.980).

Mechanics pass: run_labs PASS; twin == page; output == expected; independent per-study implementation reproduces all rows (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify7-L05-L06/scripts/lab5_indep.py); BH rows equal L03 Lab 3 digit for digit; seeded; Pyodide 0.7 s. The hypothesis says 'The uncorrected constants (3) have no guarantee from this lesson in this design: the shared shock ties the true-null statistics to the false-null ones, so condition (27) fails', and the interpretation says 'The low exceedance of the uncorrected constants is evidence about this design, not a guarantee.' Both are wrong. (i) At rho = 0 there is no shared shock (sqrt(0) W = 0): all p-values are independent, condition (27) holds, and Lehmann-Romano Theorem 3.1 (stated on this page, line 592) guarantees the uncorrected constants. (ii) At rho = 0.5 and 0.8 the true-null statistics are equicorrelated normals with nonnegative correlation, whose precision matrix has nonpositive off-diagonals (checked: -0.333 and -0.952 for a 5x5 block), so they are MTP2; the one-sided p-values are coordinatewise decreasing transforms, still MTP2; and Lehmann and Romano state right after their Theorem 3.2 that 'Sarkar and Chang [11] and Sarkar [10] have shown that the Simes inequality holds for the family of distributions which is characterized by the multivariate positive of order 2 condition' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify7-L05-L06/dl/arxiv/lr2005.txt). By Theorem 7.5 (LR 3.2(ii)), quoted on this page, the uncorrected constants are therefore guaranteed at alpha in every row of this design. Monte Carlo of the Simes probability for the 450 true nulls (20,000 draws each): 0.0493 (rho 0), 0.0255 (0.5), 0.0169 (0.8), all <= 0.05 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify7-L05-L06/scripts/simes.py). The lab thus tells students a guarantee is absent where the lesson's own cited theorem supplies one, and its design cannot show the cost of dropping the correction.
